Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines

Priya,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the MSA redlines. Attached is our annotated order form and a short memo from our procurement team. High level: Avery cannot accept a broad "right to defend" for all third-party IP claims because we need the ability to participate in defense decisions when our proprietary data or integrations are involved.

That said, we're open to a compromise that keeps commercial risk limited for both sides. Proposed points we highlighted in the attached PDF:
- Narrow scope where Redwood can assume defense (claims arising solely from model code or infra defects).
- Where customer data/prompting is implicated, require a mutual defense framework and joint selection of counsel.
- A notice and evidence window of 30 days for initial triage; beyond that we expect Redwood to maintain electronic evidence retention for 2 years.
- A cap calibrated to the order value for third-party IP claims (we proposed 3x ARR).

Can you send through Redwood's operational checklist for how evidence will be captured and who the evidence custodian would be? We need that before the next legal review.

Tom
Legal, Avery Health

Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA + Order Form redlines (Avery) — proposed language + checklist

Thanks Priya — drafted a short compromise and an operational checklist outline below. High-level approach: keep defense assumption narrow, require cooperation and joint counsel selection where customer data or prompts materially contributed, and include a short appendix that describes evidence custody and SLAs (not intended to be a separate SOW).

Proposed contract paragraph (2 sentences):
"For third-party claims alleging infringement arising solely from Redwood's model implementation or infrastructure, Redwood shall have the right, at its option, to assume defense and control of such claim. For claims that allege infringement arising from Customer-provided prompts, data, integrations, or Customer modifications, the parties shall cooperate in the defense and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to agree on counsel; absent agreement, each party may select counsel and the parties shall coordinate to avoid unnecessary duplication of fees."

Operational appendix items (to attach to order form):
- Evidence custodian: Redwood Security (security@redwood.com) will provision a secure evidence bucket; retain logs and inference traces for 24 months by default.
- Triage timings: initial notice window = 30 calendar days from Customer notice; Redwood provides initial triage (collection of logs, model inputs/outputs, infra metrics) within 7 business days of notice.
- Proof package contents: request transcript of prompts, model config hash, deployment image id, request IDs, and relevant infra logs.
- Privilege & access: evidence delivery via secure transfer link; privileged communications preserved; engineering access is ticketed and scoped.
- Insurance/Cap language: propose cap = 3x annual contract value for third-party IP claims; defense-assumption claims excluded from cap where Redwood is found solely responsible due to code/infra defects.

A few comments: we should avoid indefinite evidence retention commitments (limit to 24 months unless enterprise terms apply). Also, the "absent agreement" counsel-selection backstop is important to avoid deadlock.

I'll attach this to a response to Avery — Priya, if you want to soften any of the wording for commercial reasons, flag the lines to me.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Tom / Elena — thanks for the redlines and for the collaborative tone. Based on internal review we've prepared a short compromise and an operational appendix for the order form. Summary below and attached as a one-page appendix.

Summary of proposed compromise:
- Redwood to assume defense only for third-party IP claims that arise solely from Redwood's code or infrastructure; those claims are excluded from the indemnity cap.
- For claims where Customer data, prompts, or Customer-controlled integrations are alleged to have contributed to the claim, parties will adopt a mutual defense approach with good-faith efforts to agree on counsel; if no agreement, each side may appoint counsel and coordinate to minimize duplication.
- Notice window: 30 calendar days for initial triage; Redwood will produce a first evidence snapshot within 7 business days and retain logs/traces for 24 months by default.
- Cap: propose cap = 3x annual contract value for third-party IP claims; we are open to a structured escrow/insurance obligation as an alternative for larger deals.

Operational appendix attached: includes evidence custodian contact (security@redwood.com), forensics kickoff timeline (48-hour call), first snapshot SLA (5 business days), and optional add-on fees for extended retention or in-depth engineering support.

Next steps: 
1) If this reads directionally OK, can you confirm and we'll produce a clean tracked-change MSA paragraph and the appendix for signature?
2) If Avery wants an escrow/insurance route instead of a cap, let us know and we can surface options with procurement (we can also provide insurer contacts).

I've attached the one-page appendix and the revised paragraph for quick review. We can also set up a 30-minute call Friday to walk legal/procurement through the operational checklist.

Thanks,
